name: Guinea-Bissau
headline: Guinea-Bissau: +5.8% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 75% of GDP
sections: Guinea-Bissau is a $2.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 188th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.8% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,293 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.6% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.7% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 2.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 75% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −6.7% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −6.2% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 41% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 66% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 64.3 years (2024). Population: 2.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
